subsystems.name: Propellant storage and thermal control
subsystems.role: Keeps cryogenic propellants (liquid hydrogen, oxygen or methane) cold and liquid for months or years.

subsystems.name: Fluid transfer and coupling
subsystems.role: Connects a tanker or client spacecraft to the hub and moves propellant between tanks without leaks.

subsystems.name: Robotic servicing and assembly
subsystems.role: Performs autonomous inspection, maintenance, and module assembly in orbit.

subsystems.name: Rendezvous and navigation
subsystems.role: Guides tankers to the hub and enables precise docking.

subsystems.name: Power and avionics
subsystems.role: Provides electricity, computing and communications for the hub.

subsystems.name: Structural bus and shielding
subsystems.role: Holds all modules together and protects against debris and radiation.

buildSteps.title: Design and ground testing
buildSteps.detail: Validate cryogenic fluid transfer, zero-boil-off storage, and docking in vacuum chambers that mimic space.

buildSteps.title: Launch hub modules
buildSteps.detail: Send storage tanks, power systems, and robotics to low Earth orbit on commercial rockets.

buildSteps.title: Robotic assembly in orbit
buildSteps.detail: Join the modules into a functional hub using robotic arms or astronaut spacewalks.

buildSteps.title: Install thermal control and propellant systems
buildSteps.detail: Connect tanks, cryocoolers, and transfer lines, and integrate avionics.

buildSteps.title: Commissioning and leak checks
buildSteps.detail: Pressurize the system, verify no leaks, and test all avionics and robotic functions.

buildSteps.title: First tanker docking and transfer
buildSteps.detail: A robotic tanker docks with the hub and transfers propellant into its storage tanks.

buildSteps.title: Demonstrate satellite refueling
buildSteps.detail: A client satellite docks or is serviced to receive propellant, proving the end-to-end service.

buildSteps.title: Expand to cislunar space
buildSteps.detail: Replicate the hub at a Lagrange point or lunar orbit to support deep-space missions.

prerequisites.why: Demonstrated on the ISS by NASA's Robotic Refueling Mission, but not yet at operational scale.
Zero-boil-off systems have been tested on the ground and in short space experiments, but not for years.
Used routinely by cargo spacecraft such as SpaceX Dragon and Northrop Grumman Cygnus to reach the ISS.
Demonstrated on the ISS with Canadarm2 and the Robotic Refueling Mission, but not for refueling hubs.
Commercial rockets can deliver large modules to low Earth orbit.
Chemical and electric thrusters are already used for orbital maneuvers and station-keeping.

pathway.milestone: Ground and ISS demonstrations of cryogenic transfer and robotic refueling (NASA's Robotic Refueling Mission)
pathway.unlocks: Confidence in the key technologies needed for a depot.

pathway.milestone: Dedicated LEO demonstration of a propellant depot with a robotic tanker
pathway.unlocks: Proof of end-to-end refueling in orbit.

pathway.milestone: Operational LEO hub refueling commercial satellites
pathway.unlocks: Extended satellite lifetimes and lower cost per mission.

pathway.milestone: Hub at a Lagrange point or cislunar space
pathway.unlocks: Reusable deep-space tugs and crewed missions to the Moon and Mars.
